estimand: weekly units sold of a product given its price relative to its own reference price and its recent sales (an association: prices were set by the retailer, not randomised)
population: products of one UK online gift retailer

test_new_products.definition: test weeks of products that are not eligible in training but have sales in at least 4 validation weeks (reported)

B1_recent_mean.complexity: baseline: mean of the previous 4 weeks

selection.rule: E4: among candidates with compute <= 100 us/row, order by the validation primary metric (ties within 1e-4 to the simpler); keep the first unless its validation long-horizon measure is worse than the smallest one with a paired cluster-bootstrap 95% interval of the difference entirely above 0; keep a simple baseline instead if it is strictly better on test
selection.reason: selected on validation and confirmed on test: no simple baseline is better; rejected for long-horizon drift: ['M2_gbdt']

rule_comparison.mapping: the population's purchase decision (pop.decision.purchase) scales purchase probability through price_ratio = (willingness to pay - price) / willingness to pay with coefficient 1.4; mapped with willingness to pay = the product's reference price: predicted units = B1_recent_mean units x sigmoid(z0 + 1.4 * pr) / sigmoid(z0 + 1.4 * pr_ref), pr = 1 - exp(log_rel_price), pr_ref = 0, z0 = the decision's bias plus its other terms at the population's mean preferences (relevance 0.5, goal_buy 0, wallet_cover_log 0, price_sensitivity 0.5, resource_satisfaction 0.5, belief_shops 0.5, impulsiveness 0.5)

identification_note: Observational: retailer-set prices; demand shocks that cause re-pricing (season, clearance) confound the price association.
extrapolation_limits: UCI Online Retail II, one UK online gift-ware retailer (many wholesale customers), 2009-12..2011-12, 2561 products with sales in at least 20 training weeks. The simulator may use this model for the weekly demand of a durable consumer product in an online shop given its recent sales and its price relative to its own usual price. It may NOT infer: (1) a causal price elasticity: prices were set by the retailer (seasonal re-pricing, clearance, promotions), so the price coefficient is an association and may be biased in either direction; (2) demand for services, subscriptions or digital goods; (3) competition between shops or substitution between products (not modelled); (4) prices far from a product's usual price (log relative prices outside the training quantiles); (5) other markets or years. Quantity discounts are excluded from the price by using retail-size lines (<= 12 units).
